key_insight: Parallel pairwise entangling gates across neighboring trapped-ion wells could enable efficient transversal controlled-Z operations for fault-tolerant quantum computing.
engineering_relevance: For selected register sizes, geometric cancellation can make parallel gates faster than sequential two-qubit gates while requiring a substantially lower two-photon Rabi frequency.
method: Implement simultaneous pairwise entangling operations in a double-well trapped-ion architecture.
Suppress unwanted couplings using tailored dynamical decoupling with quadratic pulse-count scaling.
Incorporate geometric cancellation to reduce the required pulse count.
evidence_signal: The study analyzes decoherence and laser-misalignment crosstalk, then evaluates crosstalk-induced errors in fault-tolerant logical Bell-state preparation using two [[4,1,2]] code blocks.
watch_item: Performance remains sensitive to decoherence and laser alignment, and the reported speed advantage applies only to selected register sizes.
paper_title: Parallel transversal entangling gates for fault-tolerant trapped-ion quantum computing
